procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay at Aurangabad
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and Order dated 13.12.2021 in CC No.1 of 2019 and CRLA No. 810 of 2019, convicting Digambar (Accused No. 1) and Mohan (Accused No. 2) for the offence punishable under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 read with Section 34 IPC.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court convicted Digambar and Mohan under Section 302 read with Section 34 of the IPC.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: Digambar (Accused No. 1) filed Criminal Appeals Nos. 221-222 of 2022. Mohan (Accused No. 2) filed Criminal Appeal No. 280 of 2023. Mohan's appeal was dismissed. The appeals were partly allowed.

issue.issue_text: Whether interference is warranted with the concurrent findings of the Trial Court and the High Court that the accused appellants are guilty of the offence punishable under Section 302 of the IPC.

facts: The appellants, Digambar and Mohan, were found guilty of an offence punishable under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) by the Trial Court.
The Bombay High Court, in its judgment dated 13th December 2021, confirmed the conviction.
The appellants challenged these concurrent findings of guilt before the Supreme Court.
The appellants' counsel argued that the conviction was based on weak evidence, such as an unreliable extra-judicial confession and the theory of 'last seen together' without sufficient corroboration.
law: Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) prescribes the punishment for murder.
The Supreme Court generally does not interfere with concurrent findings of fact by a Trial Court and a High Court unless there is a serious error or miscarriage of justice.
application: The Supreme Court heard arguments from the counsel for both the appellants and the State.
The Court stated that it had scrutinized the material evidence on record with the assistance of the learned counsel.
After reviewing the evidence and considering the arguments, the Court found no reason to disagree with the conclusions reached by both the Trial Court and the High Court.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that no interference was warranted with the concurrent findings of the Trial Court and the High Court. It therefore upheld the conviction of the appellants for the offence punishable under Section 302 of the IPC.

arguments.issue_text: Whether interference is warranted with the concurrent findings of the Trial Court and the High Court that the accused appellants are guilty of the offence punishable under Section 302 of the IPC.
appellant_arguments: The extra-judicial confession should not have been relied upon for the conviction.
Apart from the extra-judicial confession, there is absolutely no evidence to convict the appellants.
It is improbable that both the appellants and the two deceased travelled on one motorcycle.
The conviction could not be based only on the evidence of last seen together without any corroboration.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution case mainly rests on the circumstances of the accused being lastly seen in the company of the deceased, and the death of the deceased occurring shortly thereafter.
The Accused rushed to the Bhokar Police Station and himself lodged the FIR No. 404/2007, admitting that he has committed the aforesaid crime.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The awarding of a life sentence is the rule and the death sentence is an exception, and the application of the 'rarest of rare' principle is dependent upon and differs from case to case.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: After scrutinizing the material evidence on record, the Court found that no interference was warranted with the concurrent findings of the Trial Court and the High Court that the accused appellants are guilty of the offence punishable under Section 302 of the IPC.
why_appellant_lost: The Court found no reason to interfere with the concurrent findings of guilt by the Trial Court and the High Court.
why_respondent_won: The Court upheld the concurrent findings of the Trial Court and the High Court that the accused appellants were guilty.
